assumptions.description: Task-derived mechanics:3000equal-weight complete rows represent the named labweight-weighted analytical distribution, age20-79, female0/1, unique integer labels. These are not observed patients or national-population estimates.

ASSUMED target covariate law: age is20+59*Beta(1.35,1.75); female probability logistic(0.16+0.06*(age-50)/10). No target demographic values supplied or inferred. Dependence is explicitly weakly age-varying, not inferred independence.

ASSUMED conditional BMI: lognormal with log median log(26.5)+0.02*a-0.012*a^2+0.025*female, a=(age-50)/10, log SD0.18; rejection outside12-65kg/m2. All BMI location, spread, age and sex dependencies are assumptions, not recovered target statistics.

ASSUMED joint conditional BP location: SBP126+5.5*a+1.0*a^2-4*female+0.7754*(BMI-25); DBP79+1.8*a-0.7*a^2-2.5*female+0.5967*(BMI-25). Nonlinear age patterns permit later-life divergence; numeric age/sex/intercept parameters are not source-adjusted effects. Source age-group contrasts are descriptive context only.

Reported INTERSALT per-kg/m2 slopes are used as conditional BMI coefficients, assuming transport from1980s multi-country ages20-59, richer sodium/potassium/alcohol adjustment and inverse-variance pooling to this2013 selected Brazilian age20-79 analytical distribution. No age/BMI interaction is assumed. Treatment and omitted-variable differences can invalidate this. The requested linear age-adjusted regression need not equal these conditional coefficients because age is nonlinear and joint rejection can shift moments.

ASSUMED conditional Gaussian BP disturbances: SD_SBP=13+0.08*(age-20), SD_DBP=10.5mmHg, conditional rho=0.55. Rho is an explicitly assumed residual parameter, not the derived Beijing raw r. Beijing raw moments offer broad context only; conditional dependence is unidentified. Heteroscedasticity and nonlinear-age residuals imply the requested OLS residual r need not equal0.55.

ASSUMED joint support: BMI12-65; BP proposals are rejected jointly until60<=SBP<=290,30<=DBP<=200 and SBP>DBP. BP validity bounds represent analytical selection; positive PP is an additional feasibility assumption. Conditional redraw keeps covariates fixed, assuming their law already represents the selected population. No clipping or boundary mass; this changes the pre-selection Gaussian law and can alter slopes. Weight/height are not output and their separate selection effects are absorbed into the assumed BMI law; the BMI interval is compatible with at least one valid height/weight pair but not a reconstruction of their distribution.

Source-to-target transport assumes measured BMI and final seated BP have comparable units, but does not assert device equivalence. Target uses three G-TECH MA100 readings two minutes apart after>=5min rest, usually leftarm; released final averaging rule is unknown. INTERSALT averages two random-zero readings, Beijing two Omron readings; no separately estimated measurement correction is available. Residual scales integrate biological and protocol variation. BP/anthropometry remain baseline, not later lab-visit outcomes.

Target excludes reported pregnancy only and includes treatment, diabetes and hypertension. Those features are marginalized rather than explicitly generated. Source selection and treatment prevalence differ; pregnancy exclusion, lab participation and labweight effects are unknown transport assumptions. No causal or individual-recovery claim.

Equal-weight arithmetic means, sample SD(ddof1), and Pearson correlations on generated age>=65 rows are diagnostic comparisons only. Beijing source age>=65 extends beyond target age79; source weighting/SD conventions and missingness details remain unverified. SD-derived r assumes paired observations and common variance convention. No strict source replay or target validation is claimed.

Independent generator residual draws and fixed seeds describe conditional Monte Carlo variability only. Model/evidence/transport uncertainty is not quantified by repeated draws.128 rejection rounds is a finite computational safeguard; failure raises an error and never inserts clipped/fallback values.
